observations.classification: Existing historical native adapter contract and previous /root/hair_ops source observation, independently expanded; no new unique product defect.

evidence.contract: Remote derive parses the type and generates a repr(transparent) wrapper containing the typed Remote, dispatches according to reflect shape, and offers references to that Remote.
For active struct/tuple/enum fields with remote attributes, generated compile-time assertion assigns the field type to the remote wrapper associated Remote type; opaque has no such field assertions.
General Reflect dispatch requests assertion generation.
The assertion generator routes into generate_remote_assertions.
Remote definition type checks declared struct fields or enum variants; opaque branch has no fields to compare.
The current elapsed wrapper names AnimationElapsed and declares opaque reflection with transparent Serde.
The current fraction wrapper names UnitInterval with the same attributes.
The named elapsed owner has private f32 storage, finite nonnegative checked construction, and try_from-based Serde annotation.
The named fraction owner has private f32 storage, finite inclusive [0,1] checked construction and try_from-based Serde annotation.
Current DirectControlState and SprintInputState reference the two named remote reflection wrappers for typed fields.

observations.reasoning: The generated public field and mutable remote reference expose the typed owner itself; they are not inherently a raw-f32 setter. Type-equality and definition checks do not by themselves validate values, prove the invariant of all existing remote instances, or resolve every native unsafe use. The generated assertion helper functions contain None.unwrap solely as type-check scaffolding in the inspected generator; no execution of those functions is established.
observations.conditions_and_limits: Project source declares the wrappers and fields, but no project build, feature activation, expansion, actual reflective apply or deserialization, all owner construction routes, custom overrides, or product runtime behavior was examined. This is not blanket soundness of generic remote wrappers or a project failure.

Historical 059 q2332/q3445 remain open. 774 RIG-ADMISSION03-F007 concerns separate FurnitureKey construction and is not automatically this issue.
observations.future_direction: Continue auditing each actual owner’s admission, mutation, Serde and reflection use at its owning boundary. Retain opaque and typed-value distinctions; investigate any demonstrated bypass as its own first failed contract.

evidence.contract: RemoteArgs parses a syn::TypePath; definition generation unconditionally unwraps its conversion to expression path; that conversion returns syn::Error for a parenthesized final path segment.

observations.reasoning: If a successfully parsed RemoteArgs TypePath with a parenthesized final path segment reaches definition generation, the returned error is unwrapped instead of propagated into a structured diagnostic. The pinned syn parser behavior and valid supported Rust type syntax for that condition have not been inspected; its actual reachability is therefore explicitly open.

nonfindings: Public remote typed-value projection is not by itself a primitive backing-field write or proof of bypass for the two inspected private-f32 owners.
Registration selectively inserts metadata and optional dependency code; omitted automatic FromReflect is not itself a defect.
Generated assertion bodies are compile-time type-check helpers in the inspected source; their syntactic None.unwrap is not an observed runtime panic.
open_questions: Is a parenthesized final syn TypePath accepted and meaningful for reflect_remote, and can its error-conversion unwrap be reached from supported inputs?
Which actual enabled project builds invoke these derives and reflection consumers, and do other owner construction/mutation/Serde routes preserve their contracts?
Do custom remote wrappers, custom reflection overrides, nonopaque field projections, or unsafe native callers preserve their own type and layout invariants?
Are any prior FurnitureKey or geometry contracts exact aliases after current source owners and concrete callers are reconciled?

lenses.assessment: Native compiler attribute identifiers and diagnostic/type paths are framework grammar; no application magic-string defect established.
Line-level indices are compiler field positions and generic traversal, not interchangeable application quantities; no range-owner defect established.
AnimationElapsed and UnitInterval own semantic bounds; native reflected wrapper and registry metadata are adapters, not substitute validation authorities.
Current wrappers target existing checked owners and typed DirectControlState fields instead of newly storing primitive f32 authority.
Struct, tuple, enum and opaque branches have distinct generator shapes; opaque whole-remote projection differs from active-field assertions.
Mutable remote projection exposes a typed owner; whether its own public methods and other construction paths preserve validity remains independently open.
Remote field assertion relates wrapper associated Remote type to field type; it does not assert cross-field or whole-value application invariants.
Opaque projection can preserve already admitted values but cannot establish how each remote value was constructed or whether its later mutation is valid.
Enum and struct branches are independently selected; the definition checker emits shape/type comparisons, with no assessment of all application variant-state policies.
The wrapper stores the existing typed Remote and registration stores metadata, rather than duplicating a primitive state; wider registry lifecycle remains outside scope.
Any future change must respect supported opaque behavior, checked owner constructors, explicit registration opt-outs and no backwards-compatibility shims.
Current field declarations connect two specific wrapper names to typed project fields; runtime use, feature selection, and other callers are not inferred.
Generated registration and remote adapters are justified when their native contracts match the owner; checked Serde/opaque attributes are not redundant merely because derives exist.

limitations: Two pinned native package files personally read in full; all support exactly bounded. No complete Bevy package, product graph, all features, whole-lens completion, macro expansion, compilation, build, tests, execution, runtime probes, repair or product validation.
